title: adaptive-perf-profile-refresh-via-sampled-production-shadowing
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: We maintain Redwood-verified performance profiles (latency, throughput, cost) for models used across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Profiles drift when serving runtime changes, model variants are updated, or real-world input distributions diverge. Current refreshes are largely offline and periodic which leads to stale pins and conservative rollouts.

Objective: Implement an adaptive profile refresh pipeline that uses sampled production shadow traffic and lightweight runtime-side probes to determine when a profile should be regenerated, and automate a staggered publish with safety checks and rollback hooks. The goal is to reduce stale profile windows, keep pins accurate to real-world latency/cost, and lower manual triage while minimizing customer risk.

Scope:
- Implement sampling and shadowing hooks to mirror a small fraction of live requests to a sandboxed verification harness.
- Collect runtime-aware metrics: tail latency, p50/p95, throughput under production batching, KV cache hit/miss, and token-cost delta normalized by batching.
- Define statistical triggers for profile degeneration and automated generation of candidate profiles.
- Automate staggered publish (regional canary -> cohort canary -> global) with rollback criteria tied to regression thresholds and business metrics.

Out of scope for this ticket: automatic model retraining, changing customer-facing default pins without signoff, or deep rearchitecting of the metrics pipeline (we will extend existing telemetry).
acceptance_criteria: Sampling: 1% of production traffic can be mirrored to the verification harness without impacting production latency or cost significantly.

Measure set: verification harness collects p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, KV cache hit rate, average tokens-per-request, and normalized cost-per-token under production batching for each sampled request.
Trigger: statistical detector flags a profile when at least 3 independent windows (24h, 72h, 7d) show >10% median latency regression or >15% cost-per-token increase after normalization.
Candidate generation: system can auto-generate a candidate performance profile and publish it to a staging registry where a regional canary can be executed.

Staged publish: rollout automation performs regional canary followed by cohort canaries; if any canary exceeds rollback thresholds (p95 increase >5% or cost delta >10% or error-rate increase >0.2pp), publish is automatically aborted and reverted.

Audit & traceability: each auto-refresh run is recorded with a signed artifact, diff summary, and link to telemetry dashboards; changes require an owner signoff for global publish unless an emergency override flag is set.
Operational runbook: runbook created and reviewed by SRE and Runtime teams describing how to investigate failures and perform manual rollback or fast-forward.
Alerts: alerting created for false positives (high regeneration churn) and for missed detections (customer-facing latency regressions not captured).
tasks: PM: finalize trigger thresholds and acceptance criteria with Runtime and SRE stakeholders
Eng: implement request mirror hook and lightweight verifier container for sampled traffic
Eng: extend telemetry to emit normalized cost and kv-cache metrics to verification pipeline
Eng: build candidate profile generator and diff artifact signer
Eng: implement staged publish automation (regional -> cohort -> global) and rollback hooks
Design: update profile registry UI to surface candidate diffs, signoffs, and canary statuses in Console
SRE: author runbook and define alert thresholds
Compliance: review audit trail requirements for Private deployments (VPC/on-prem)
progress_updates: 2025-02-25: Scoping session with Runtime, SRE, and Observability. Agreement on metric set and sampling budget (default 0.5% - 2% configurable per org).

2025-03-01: Prototype mirror implemented in sandbox; initial verifier container captures latency & kv-cache hits for synthetic shadow traffic. Observed batching amplification and adjusted normalization formula.
2025-03-03: PM/Runtime tradeoff: lower sampling reduces sensitivity to short regressions; decided on multi-window detector to avoid knee-jerk refreshes. Preparing PRD for engineering sprint.
notes: Key tradeoffs: sampling budget vs detection latency; normalization for batching must account for dedicated vs hosted modes; private deployments may require special audit-only flows. We should run a 4-week pilot on non-critical model family before expanding.
